title: Controlled MCP Action Tools Foundation
goal: Plan and implement the first safe MCP action-tool slice only after read-only MCP context is validated.
scope: Add a tightly controlled MCP action-tool foundation for low-risk operator-reviewed actions such as drafting a ticket or requesting a retest proposal. Preserve approval gates and require explicit operator confirmation for state changes.
generation_reason: Product recommendation coverage audit found MCP write/action tools were intentionally deferred but not queued as a gated future package.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Action tools must be gated, explicit, and operator-reviewed. Do not add autonomous dispatch, approval bypass, deployment bypass, or secret access.
notes: Read-only MCP must be validated before this package is promoted.
Prefer proposal-producing tools before state-changing tools.

success_criteria: The first MCP action tools are limited to reviewed proposal or low-risk handoff actions.
Any state-changing action requires explicit operator confirmation and existing authorization checks.
Approval, dispatch, pack deployment, and runtime binding gates remain intact.
Tests cover allowed, denied, unauthenticated, and confirmation-required paths.
Docs list permitted and forbidden MCP actions.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding bypasses

acceptance_criteria: MCP actions are gated and operator-reviewed.
Forbidden runtime, approval, and secret actions are blocked.
Existing platform gates are reused, not bypassed.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
Read-only MCP baseline is completed and permitted action list is approved.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with MCP action-tool changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with MCP action-tool baseline and remaining action limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
